subject: Mathematics
name: Foundation Mathematics, Units 1 and 2
about: VCE, Everyday number, money, data and measurement
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), Foundation Mathematics Units 1 and 2

units.title: Unit 1: Number, data, money and measurement

points.title: Order of operations
points.brief: Brackets, then powers, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right.

points.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages
points.brief: The same amount written three ways, such as 1/4, 0.25 and 25%, and moving between them.

points.title: Percentages of amounts
points.brief: Find a percentage of an amount by multiplying, such as 15% of $80 is 0.15 × 80 = $12.

points.title: Ratios and rates
points.brief: A ratio compares amounts of the same kind, such as 2:3. A rate compares different units, such as km per hour.

points.title: Estimating and rounding
points.brief: Rounding to a sensible place and estimating first catches errors, such as a calculator answer ten times too big.

points.title: Collecting data
points.brief: Surveys, measurements and observations collect data. A biased sample can give a wrong picture.

points.title: Reading tables and graphs
points.brief: Reading values, trends and comparisons from tables, bar graphs, line graphs and pie charts.

points.title: Drawing charts and graphs
points.brief: Choosing and drawing a column graph, line graph, pie chart or table that fits the data, with a title, labels and scale.

points.title: Misleading graphs
points.brief: Graphs mislead with axes that do not start at zero, uneven scales or pictures sized unfairly.

points.title: Pay and payslips
points.brief: Working out pay from an hourly rate, overtime and penalty rates or a salary, and reading what a payslip shows.

points.title: Banking, bills and borrowing
points.brief: Bank accounts, card payments, paying bills on time and what borrowing costs, for everyday money tasks.

points.title: Tax and superannuation
points.brief: Income tax comes out of pay, and employers pay superannuation into a fund for retirement, both as a share of earnings.

points.title: Tax and the community
points.brief: Taxes pay for shared services such as roads, schools and hospitals, collected by local, state and federal governments.

points.title: Fees and interest
points.brief: Account fees, late fees and simple interest add to costs. Simple interest is the amount times the rate times the time.

points.title: Discounts and mark-ups
points.brief: A 20% discount multiplies the price by 0.8. A 20% mark-up multiplies it by 1.2.

points.title: Units and converting
points.brief: Converting between mm, cm, m and km, between g and kg, and between mL and L.

points.title: Reading scales
points.brief: Reading measuring jugs, scales, thermometers, gauges and digital displays accurately, to the nearest marked unit.

points.title: Perimeter and area in practice
points.brief: Working out lengths of fencing or areas of flooring, including composite shapes.

points.title: Volume and capacity
points.brief: Volume of rectangular prisms and cylinders, and that 1000 cm³ holds 1 L.

points.title: Time and timetables
points.brief: 24-hour time, time differences and reading timetables to plan a trip.

units.title: Unit 2: Formulas, data, money and space

points.title: Patterns and rules
points.brief: Writing a pattern as a rule, such as cost = 4 × number of tickets, lets you work out any value.

points.title: Using formulas
points.brief: Substituting values into a formula, such as cost = 40 + 25 × hours, to work out a result.

points.title: Solving simple equations
points.brief: Undoing operations in reverse order to find an unknown, such as 3x + 5 = 20.

points.title: Mean, median and spread
points.brief: The mean and median give a typical value; the range and interquartile range show how spread out the data is.

points.title: Comparing data sets
points.brief: Putting two sets of data side by side, such as two teams' scores, with graphs and summary numbers, to draw a fair conclusion.

points.title: Comparing products
points.brief: Comparing price per unit, features and terms, such as across phone plans or health products, to make an informed choice.

points.title: Personal budgets
points.brief: A budget lists income and expenses so spending stays within income and savings goals can be met.

points.title: Planning for life stages
points.brief: Money needs change from school to work, renting, family and retirement, so plans change too.

points.title: Study debts and government support
points.brief: HECS-HELP loans are repaid through tax once income passes a threshold. Payments such as child-care support reduce costs.

points.title: Financial trends
points.brief: Data on prices (CPI), interest rates, wages and house prices over time shows how costs and incomes are changing.

points.title: Shapes and objects
points.brief: Naming and describing simple and composite shapes and objects by their sides, angles, faces and edges.

points.title: Reading plans and diagrams
points.brief: House plans and diagrams use scales and symbols to show real sizes and layouts.

points.title: Scale and maps
points.brief: A scale such as 1:50 000 turns map distances into real distances.

points.title: Routes and travel times
points.brief: Planning a route with maps or apps, using distance and speed to estimate how long a trip will take.
